label: token right after an n at original positions 3-5
explanation: Fires during the original (input) phase on the step immediately after the letter n, when that step is at position 4-6, i.e. the n sat at original position 3-5. This one condition has precision 0.96 and covers about 87% of activation mass, including nearly all of the top two activation quartiles. The current input token barely matters; it can even be a second n. Activation is strongest at t=4-5, and the top examples (around 2.9) are an n at position 3 followed by another token at t=5 after a repeated n. Many steps fire weakly and are missed (recall 0.58): the step two after an n, which also decays, and weak firings after 1, f or c at similar positions. Almost never fires at t<=2 or t>=8, never fires in the copy phase, and fires only weakly at the delimiter. An n at position 6 or later (the step after it at t>=7) rarely fires.

issues: Reproduced the test scores exactly: P 0.962, R 0.584, F1 0.727, mass recall 0.875. Coverage by activation quartile is [0.06, 0.35, 0.93, 0.997], which backs the claim that the predicate covers nearly all of the top two quartiles.

Phase claims hold. No firing at all in the copy phase (0 of 2.73M dev steps). The delimiter carries only 1.5% of mass, and prev_tok==n at the delimiter has precision 0.14. No firing at t<=2 or t>=8, and t=7 has only 351 dev firings.

Precision varies by step. With prev_tok==n it is 1.000 at t=4, 0.998 at t=5, 0.848 at t=6, 0.194 at t=3 and 0.057 at t=7. So the 4-6 window is right, but t=6 is noticeably less reliable. At t=6, an earlier extra n in the sequence lowers precision to 0.65, but that covers only about 1.3k predicted steps, so it is a minor effect.
Two n's in a row: prev n with in_tok n at t=4-6 has precision 0.969, and n,n then fire at t=5 has precision 1.0. This fits 'can even be a second n'.

Misses (12.5% of mass) are a diffuse weak baseline, not one systematic class. Every prev_tok other than n at t=4-6 fires at a rate of 1.8%, mostly in the bottom quartiles. prev2_tok==n alone has precision 0.19, and prev_tok in {1,f,c} has precision 0.09. Adding either to the predicate lowers F1 (0.717 and 0.709 vs 0.727). The explanation already reports these weak firings and the low recall honestly.
The label does not overclaim beyond the predicate.
